npcs.name: Old Cottos
npcs.desc: A stooped man with a beard like a thornbush.

npcs.name: Bandit
npcs.desc: Hungry and armed.

npcs.name: Bandit spearman
npcs.desc: Javelins over his shoulder.

npcs.name: Wolf
npcs.desc: Grey, lean, and not afraid of you.

npcs.name: Brigand
npcs.desc: A farmer once, by the hands. Not anymore, by the eyes.

npcs.name: Brigand slinger
npcs.desc: A boy with a sling and a very good arm.

npcs.name: Refugee
npcs.desc: A man pushing a handcart with everything his family owns.

npcs.name: Refugee
npcs.desc: A woman carrying a bundle and watching your hands.

npcs.name: Old refugee
npcs.desc: An old man who walks like every step is a decision.

npcs.name: Salt trader
npcs.desc: Thickset, good cloak, careful eyes. The mules are better fed than he is.

npcs.name: Trader's guard
npcs.desc: Bored, in a professional way.

npcs.name: Roman forager
npcs.desc: A legionary with a sack of somebody's grain over his shoulder and a sword in his other hand.

npcs.name: Balearic slinger
npcs.desc: An islander in Roman pay, three slings wound round his head and a bag of stones at his hip.

npcs.name: Matugenta
npcs.desc: Your mother. Grey at the temples since the day they took Eponina, and she has never once said so.

npcs.name: Vellaunos
npcs.desc: Chief of the elders. A big man gone thin, with a voice that still fills the hall.

npcs.name: Cobnertos the smith
npcs.desc: Forearms like oak roots and burn scars to the elbow. His son is the second hostage.

npcs.name: Cintugnatos
npcs.desc: The vates: seer, healer, keeper of the shrine. Young for it, and knows that everyone thinks so.

npcs.name: Moccos
npcs.desc: Keeper of the gate. Old enough to have fought the Romans once and lost, young enough to want to again.

npcs.name: Villager
npcs.desc: Someone you have known all your life.

npcs.name: Villager
npcs.desc: Someone you have known all your life.

npcs.name: Young warrior
npcs.desc: One of the young men who wants a war and has never seen one.

npcs.name: Dubnacos
npcs.desc: Home again, and not sure yet what that means.

npcs.name: Dubnacos
npcs.desc: Thin, quick, a good sword and a bad cloak. Exiled from Brigodunon three winters ago for a killing.

npcs.name: Outlaw
npcs.desc: A man the world has no use for, and who has noticed.

npcs.name: Outlaw slinger
npcs.desc: A boy with a sling and an old man's eyes.

npcs.name: Sulicena
npcs.desc: Headwoman of Vindomagos. Counts everything twice, and smiles once you are worth it.

npcs.name: Lugurix the salt merchant
npcs.desc: White to the elbows with salt dust. Knows the price of everything from here to the sea.

npcs.name: Old Banna
npcs.desc: The village healer. Hands like roots, eyes like a hawk.

npcs.name: Villager
npcs.desc: A farmer of Vindomagos.

npcs.name: Villager
npcs.desc: A farmer of Vindomagos.

npcs.name: Haldo
npcs.desc: Leader of the horsemen at the ford. Fair hair knotted on the side of his head, a Roman mail shirt, and a Gallic shield he took from somebody.

npcs.name: Germanic rider
npcs.desc: One of Caesar's Germanic horse, from across the Rhenus. Now nobody's.

npcs.name: Germanic rider
npcs.desc: Keeps his bow strung and his eyes on you.

npcs.name: Carter from Vindomagos
npcs.desc: Sitting on a cart of grain sacks with the patience of a man paid by the day.

npcs.name: Theron
npcs.desc: A Greek from Massilia: soft hands, quick eyes, a good cloak kept carefully shabby. Speaks Gallic better than most Gauls and Latin better than most Romans, and says so.

npcs.name: Paconius
npcs.desc: A thin man in a Gallic cloak and Gallic trousers, with a Roman haircut that is growing out as fast as it can. Ink in the creases of his fingers.

npcs.name: Vercingetorix
npcs.desc: Young for a king, and not tall, and it doesn't matter: the room arranges itself around him. A heavy gold torc, a plain mail shirt, and the stillness of a man who has already decided.

npcs.name: King's guard
npcs.desc: One of the young nobles who rode with Vercingetorix when he had nothing. Mail, a long sword, and no sense of humor about the king.

npcs.name: Ollognatos
npcs.desc: The king's hostage-master. He counts the children the peoples of Gaul send to Gergovia, and the spears. Grey at the temples, a tally stick behind each ear, and very tired.

npcs.name: Ategnatos
npcs.desc: An old Arvernian noble of the uncle's party, the ones who said wait. He wasn't thrown out with the others. He has been wondering why ever since.

npcs.name: Eppillos
npcs.desc: Ategnatos's son, nineteen or twenty, at the bottom of a pit with his hands tied in front of him. He has stopped shouting.

npcs.name: Pit guard
npcs.desc: A spearman with a cold, watching a hole in the ground for the king.

npcs.name: Hostage
npcs.desc: Somebody's son, sent to Gergovia so that his people will keep their word. Well fed, well dressed, and not allowed past the fence.

npcs.name: Hostage
npcs.desc: Somebody's daughter, sent to Gergovia so that her people will keep their word. Well fed, well dressed, and not allowed past the fence.

npcs.name: Senognatos
npcs.desc: Captain of the levy camp below the wall. He shouts for a living, and has the voice to show for it.

npcs.name: Levy man
npcs.desc: One of the poor men Vercingetorix raised in the countryside: a herdsman or a debtor or a runaway, with a spear the king gave him and nothing else.

npcs.name: Townsman
npcs.desc: An Arvernian of the lower town.

npcs.name: Townswoman
npcs.desc: An Arvernian of the lower town.

npcs.name: Excingos the smith
npcs.desc: Black to the shoulders, burnt in a dozen places, and working faster than anyone should have to. The king wants spearheads. The king always wants spearheads.

npcs.name: Nammia
npcs.desc: Sells bread, mead and gossip from a trestle under an awning. Her prices go up every time a rider comes in from the north.

npcs.name: Uxellos the potter
npcs.desc: A potter with clay to the elbows and opinions about everyone. His yard backs onto the palisade.

npcs.name: Man by the road
npcs.desc: He keeps his hood up. Under it, where his ears were, are two healing wounds.

npcs.name: Gate guard
npcs.desc: Watches the gate in the wall, and everyone who goes through it.

npcs.name: Senodonnos
npcs.desc: One of the magistrates of Avaricum: a big, soft-spoken man with black eyebrows and a gold torque he keeps touching, as if to make sure the city is still there.

npcs.name: Epomeduos
npcs.desc: An Aeduan in a good cloak with a stylus behind his ear. He has the clean hands and patient smile of a man who is paid by the line.

npcs.name: Nertomara
npcs.desc: A widow of good family in a house too big for three. Her hands never stop: spinning, mending, counting the children.

npcs.name: Andecamulos the ironmaster
npcs.desc: Master of the city's furnaces. Burn scars to the elbow, a voice that carries over a forge, and the calm of a man who knows exactly how hot everything is.

npcs.name: Vindos the boatman
npcs.desc: A lean, weathered man who has spent his life poling a flat boat through the reeds north of the city. He knows every channel, and every channel's price.

npcs.name: Sumelis
npcs.desc: Sells everything from a stall in the forum and hears everything from behind it. She has the best memory for faces in Avaricum and charges for it.

npcs.name: Gate warden
npcs.desc: A spearman of the Bituriges on the gate, wet through and proud of his wall.

npcs.name: Townsman
npcs.desc: A Biturigan of Avaricum.

npcs.name: Townswoman
npcs.desc: A Biturigan of Avaricum.

npcs.name: Picked man
npcs.desc: One of the ten thousand the king sent into the city: hard, muddy, and sure of nothing except the man beside him.

npcs.name: Miner
npcs.desc: Clay to the eyebrows. The Bituriges have dug iron for longer than anyone remembers; now they dig for their lives.

npcs.name: Legionary
npcs.desc: A legionary in a soaked red tunic, leaning on his shield. He has been digging and fighting in the rain for a month, and it shows.

npcs.name: Hermeros
npcs.desc: A freedman of the house of Vettius, Greek by name and Roman by trade. A sun hat, a folding stool, and a day book open on his knee.

npcs.name: Captive
npcs.desc: A man of Avaricum with a rope on his wrists and a number in the Roman's book.

npcs.name: Captive
npcs.desc: A woman of Avaricum with a rope on her wrists and a number in the Roman's book.

npcs.name: Girl
npcs.desc: A girl of ten or eleven, folded small behind the grain jars, with flour in her hair and her eyes on the door.

npcs.name: Dagolitos
npcs.desc: The Aeduan keeper of the gate: a good cloak, a gold ring on every other finger, and the patient look of a man who is paid by everyone who passes.

npcs.name: Sentry
npcs.desc: A legionary on gate duty in the rain, the most boring job in the Roman army, and he knows it.

npcs.name: Watchman
npcs.desc: An Aeduan levy man hired to walk the depot at night and stand at doors by day. Paid in Roman silver and bored in two languages.

npcs.name: Watch sergeant
npcs.desc: The man in charge of the night watch, which means he walks the line twice and then sits by the forge.

npcs.name: Paymaster's clerk
npcs.desc: A Roman freedman who sits by the pay chest with a gladius across his knees and counts the same coins twice a day.

npcs.name: Naevius
npcs.desc: A Roman wine trader from Placentia who has lived among the Aedui so long he says 'we' about both, depending on who's asking.

npcs.name: Townsman
npcs.desc: An Aeduan of Noviodunum.

npcs.name: Townswoman
npcs.desc: An Aeduan of Noviodunum.

npcs.name: Lucius Orbius
npcs.desc: The quartermaster of the depot. Fifty, bald, ink on the side of his hand, a cough he's had since the autumn. He counts everything that comes in, and everything that goes out, including people.

npcs.name: Ateula
npcs.desc: Vellaunos's daughter, seventeen. A plain Roman dress, ink on her fingers, a stylus behind her ear. She looks at you the way her father does, as if weighing grain.

npcs.name: Eponina
npcs.desc: Your sister. Fourteen. Her hair is cut short like a Roman girl's and she has your mother's chin.

npcs.name: Iccios
npcs.desc: Cobnertos's son. Nineteen, broad as a door, with burn scars up both forearms. He works the depot forge and doesn't look up.

npcs.name: Neitin
npcs.desc: A horse-boy from Hispania, sixteen or so, with a groom's bent back already. He talks to the horses in a language nobody else here speaks.

npcs.name: Hostage
npcs.desc: Somebody's son, from somewhere in Gaul, kept here so his people keep their word.

npcs.name: Hostage
npcs.desc: Somebody's daughter, from somewhere in Gaul, kept here so her people keep their word.

npcs.name: Eponina
npcs.desc: Your sister, home. Her hair is growing out, badly, and she won't let anyone cut it.

npcs.name: Iccios
npcs.desc: Cobnertos's son, back at his father's anvil as if he'd never left. He has.

npcs.name: Ateula
npcs.desc: Vellaunos's daughter, home, still with ink on her fingers. She has started writing down what the elders say.

npcs.name: Senuacos
npcs.desc: The elder of Cenabum: white-bearded, a judge's staff of black wood across his knees, and the stillness of a man who has decided that whatever happens next is the gods' business.

npcs.name: Litumara
npcs.desc: A Carnute woman of thirty in a Roman-cut gown gone filthy, sitting in the straw with her arm round a small boy. She watches the door the way you'd watch a dog you don't know.

npcs.name: Boy
npcs.desc: Five or six. His mother's eyes and a Roman haircut, and two names, and he answers to both.

npcs.name: Atepomaros
npcs.desc: A big Carnute farmer in his forties with a sword he hasn't owned long. Three years ago his brother went to the Romans for a debt, and he keeps the account of it the way other men keep a grudge: exactly.

npcs.name: Kinsman
npcs.desc: One of Atepomaros's cousins, keeping the pen because he was told to.

npcs.name: Cunissos
npcs.desc: A thin man with sooty hands who has been living in the Roman traders' houses since the killing, and selling them back to the town a room at a time.

npcs.name: Onnacos
npcs.desc: A short, wide boatman with forearms like hams, mending a net on an upturned boat. He talks about the Liger as if it were a person, and not one he likes.

npcs.name: Townsman
npcs.desc: A Carnute of Cenabum.

npcs.name: Townswoman
npcs.desc: A Carnute of Cenabum.

npcs.name: Old woman
npcs.desc: An old woman sitting on the stone footing of a house that isn't there anymore, with her hands in her lap.

npcs.name: Senouindos
npcs.desc: A very old man in undyed wool, bald as an egg, with a beard he has stopped bothering to trim and eyes that have read the entrails of more bulls than you have eaten. He sits as if the grove had been planted round him.

npcs.name: Bitugenos
npcs.desc: A bard: a man of forty with a lyre on his knee and a voice that carries further than he means it to. He knows the names of everyone's grandfathers, and what each of them did wrong.

npcs.name: Toutillos
npcs.desc: A novice of fourteen or so, ink-less and book-less, mouthing verses under his breath. He has seven years of them learned and thirteen to go.

npcs.name: Pilgrim
npcs.desc: Someone who has walked a long way to have a quarrel judged.

npcs.name: Pilgrim
npcs.desc: Someone who has walked a long way to have a quarrel judged.

npcs.name: Epomeduos
npcs.desc: An Aeduan in a good cloak with a stylus behind his ear, a guest at Vellaunos's fire. He has the clean hands and patient smile of a man who is paid by the line.

npcs.name: Diodotos
npcs.desc: A freedman of the house of Vettius: a Roman tunic under a good Gallic cloak, a Greek name, and the small exact bow of a man who knows what a bow is worth.

npcs.name: Aeduan spearman
npcs.desc: One of Dannotalos's ambacti, lent to the house for the road. He has been told to keep the freedman alive and nothing else.

npcs.name: Runner
npcs.desc: A boy from Brigodunon with mud to the knees and Vellaunos's iron ring on a thong round his neck.

npcs.name: Vettius
npcs.desc: Aulus Vettius Calvus: a Roman of fifty in a plain good tunic, ink on his second finger, and eyes tired the way a lamp is tired at the end of the night.

npcs.name: Strongroom keeper
npcs.desc: A big Gaul with a slave's cropped hair and a club through his belt. He sits against the strongroom door the way a dog lies across a threshold.

npcs.name: Felix
npcs.desc: A slave clerk of the house, perhaps twenty, copying figures with the speed of somebody who is beaten for blots. His name means lucky. Somebody thought that was funny.

npcs.name: Demarchos
npcs.desc: A Greek of Massilia in a white cloak with a blue border, older and heavier than Theron and with the same quick eyes. He lends money to people who lend money.

npcs.name: Roman trader
npcs.desc: An Italian wine merchant, sunburned under his hat, who has lived on the Arar long enough to swear in Gallic.

npcs.name: Aeduan townsman
npcs.desc: An Aeduan of Cabillonum: a docker, a carter, a man who unloads Roman wine all day and doesn't get to drink it.

npcs.name: Aeduan townswoman
npcs.desc: An Aeduan woman of Cabillonum with a basket of eels and opinions about Romans.

npcs.name: Boatman
npcs.desc: A broad Aeduan boatman with a pole over his shoulder, watching the river the way other men watch the sky.

npcs.name: Dannotalos
npcs.desc: An Aeduan noble not yet thirty, with a gold torc as thick as a child's wrist and an old man's careful hands. He looks at everything in the hall, you included, the way a man looks at goods he has already priced.

npcs.name: Cingetos
npcs.desc: Dannotalos's champion: a big quiet man with a broken nose and a sword-arm scarred from wrist to elbow. At the feast he sits at his lord's right hand, and the thigh joint goes to him.

npcs.name: Dannotalos's man
npcs.desc: One of Dannotalos's ambacti: a spearman of his household who eats at his table, fights at his word, and has no other.

npcs.name: Convictolitavis
npcs.desc: The vergobret of the Aedui this year, chosen through the priests and confirmed by Caesar: a young man for the office, very well dressed, who listens with his whole face and decides somewhere behind it.

npcs.name: Esugenos
npcs.desc: A druid of the Aedui, sixty or so, in undyed wool with a bronze wheel at his throat. He keeps the spring in the middle of the town, and the town keeps its voice down near him.

npcs.name: Gate warden
npcs.desc: An Aeduan with a long spear and a helmet he polishes, at the gate through the inner bank. He has a list of the houses above in his head and a low opinion of most of the people who ask for them.

npcs.name: Gobannos the smith
npcs.desc: A smith of the craftsmen's quarter with forearms like hams and a voice ruined by smoke. Half the iron in his yard is spoken for, and he won't say by whom.

npcs.name: Enameler
npcs.desc: A woman of the craftsmen's quarter with red enamel under every fingernail, setting glass into the bosses of a harness for somebody's horse.

npcs.name: Aeduan townsman
npcs.desc: An Aeduan of Bibracte in a checked cloak, with wine on his breath and opinions about the Arverni.

npcs.name: Aeduan townswoman
npcs.desc: An Aeduan woman of Bibracte carrying a jar of Italian wine on her hip as if it were nothing much.

npcs.name: Aeduan youth
npcs.desc: A young Aeduan noble's son with a new sword and nobody yet to use it on. He talks about the Arverni loudly enough for the whole street.
